ref_extractions.title: Bimodal electroencephalography-functional magnetic resonance imaging dataset for inner-speech recognition
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This bioRxiv preprint is the original publication for the bimodal inner speech dataset. It explicitly describes the dataset with 4 subjects, 8 words in 2 categories (social and numeric), and 320 trials per participant, matching openneuro_ds004196. The paper reports baseline classification results (62.81% EEG-only for binary social vs numeric).
ref_extractions.epoch_params: window around stimulus onset; specific window not detailed in HTML preview
ref_extractions.label_mapping: social (child, daughter, father, wife) vs numeric (four, three, ten, six)
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: Abstract confirms 4 healthy right-handed participants, 8-word stimuli in social/numeric categories, 40 trials per word, 320 trials per subject. Authors report EEG-fMRI binary classification accuracy.

ref_extractions.title: Bimodal EEG-fMRI Inner Speech Dataset (preprocessing repository)
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This is the official GitHub repository containing preprocessing code for the bimodal dataset. The README links to OpenNeuro ds004197 (likely typo; should be ds004196) and cites the same bioRxiv DOI. Contains EEG preprocessing pipeline code (EEGLAB) and stimulation protocols.
ref_extractions.epoch_params: Preprocessing via EEGLAB with ICA for artifact removal; stimulus timing from E-Prime protocols
ref_extractions.super_meta_note: Repository contains stimulus timing information and preprocessing scripts that enable epoch extraction from continuous EEG data
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: README states dataset available at OpenNeuro, links to preprocessing_pipeline.m for EEG processing steps including filtering, referencing, and ICA artifact removal.

ref_extractions.title: Bimodal pilot study on inner speech decoding reveals the potential of combining EEG and fMRI
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This is the peer-reviewed version of the bimodal inner speech dataset paper published in Scientific Data. It provides comprehensive details on 1,280 total trials (4 subjects × 8 stimuli × 40 trials), binary classification results (62.81% EEG-only), and explicit social/numeric word categories with defined labels.
ref_extractions.epoch_params: EEG: 64 channels, 512 Hz, 320 trials per subject; epochs extracted from window around stimulus onset
ref_extractions.label_mapping: social (child, daughter, father, wife) = 0; numeric (four, three, ten, six) = 1
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: Reports 62.81% EEG accuracy for binary classification (chance 50%) and 22.19% for 8-class (chance 12.5%) using subject-dependent approach. Social category: child, daughter, father, wife; Numeric category: four, three, ten, six.

ref_extractions.title: Developing an IoT-Driven BCI Framework for Real-Time Neural Signal Decoding to Speech Conversion
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This chapter describes an IoT-based BCI framework using the FEIS dataset (not openneuro_ds004196) for imagined speech recognition. It focuses on phoneme classification with 14-channel Emotiv EPOC+ EEG from 21 subjects, which is a completely different dataset, electrode system, and paradigm.
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: Uses FEIS dataset with 14-channel EEG, 21 participants, phoneme-based classification (consonants and vowels), not related to bimodal inner speech dataset.

ref_extractions.title: Natural language processing methods are sensitive to sub-clinical linguistic differences in schizophrenia spectrum disorders
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This paper uses NLP methods to analyze speech samples from schizophrenia patients vs healthy controls. It uses textual speech data, not EEG recordings, and does not involve openneuro_ds004196 or any inner speech decoding task.
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: Focuses on NLP analysis of speech transcripts from SSD (n=20) vs HC (n=11) participants; uses BERT embeddings and POS tagging, no EEG data involved.

ref_extractions.title: A high-performance neuroprosthesis for speech decoding and avatar control
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This Nature paper uses ECoG (not EEG) from a single paralyzed participant with 253-channel implant for speech decoding. It is an invasive single-subject study, completely unrelated to the openneuro_ds004196 bimodal non-invasive EEG dataset with 4 healthy subjects.
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: Uses 253-channel high-density ECoG array, single tetraplegic participant, attempts silent speech of sentences, not related to 4-subject EEG-fMRI inner speech dataset.

ref_extractions.title: Thinking out loud, an open-access EEG-based BCI dataset for inner speech recognition
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This Scientific Data paper describes a separate open-access inner speech EEG dataset (by Nieto et al.) with 10 participants performing 4 mental tasks. Although related to inner speech, it is a completely different dataset from openneuro_ds004196 and was collected by different research groups.
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: Different dataset with 10 participants, 136 channels, >9 hours of continuous EEG, inner speech BCI commands - not the bimodal ds004196 with 4 subjects and EEG-fMRI.

ref_extractions.title: Bimodal electroencephalography-functional magnetic resonance imaging dataset for inner-speech recognition
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This is the official Scientific Data publication for the bimodal dataset available at openneuro_ds004196. It explicitly describes 4 healthy participants, 8-word stimuli (social/numeric categories), 40 trials per word, 320 trials per subject, and provides the complete dataset description.
ref_extractions.epoch_params: EEG: 64-channel BioSemi Active23, 512 Hz sampling rate; epochs aligned to stimulus onsets; 2 categories × 4 words × 40 trials
ref_extractions.label_mapping: social category: child, daughter, father, wife; numeric category: four, three, ten, six
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: Full dataset descriptor: 4 right-handed participants, EEG and fMRI acquired nonsimultaneously, 320 trials per modality per participant, Social vs Numeric binary classification task defined.

ref_extractions.title: Online internal speech decoding from single neurons in a human participant
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This medRxiv preprint uses invasive microelectrode recordings (not EEG) from a single tetraplegic participant implanted with arrays in SMG and S1. The participant performed internal and vocalized speech of 6 words and 2 pseudowords. This is unrelated to the non-invasive bimodal openneuro_ds004196 dataset.
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: Invasive single-unit recordings from SMG and S1 in tetraplegic participant, not openneuro_ds004196 which uses non-invasive 64-channel EEG from 4 healthy subjects.

ref_extractions.title: A mechanism for sensorimotor translation in singing: the multi-modal imagery association (MMIA) model
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This paper proposes a theoretical model for singing accuracy based on multi-modal imagery associations. It uses MEG for mental imagery of speech and finger tapping but does not use the openneuro_ds004196 dataset or perform any inner speech classification task.
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: Theoretical paper on singing and imagery using MEG; involves different researchers, methodology, and experimental goals unrelated to inner speech EEG classification.

ref_extractions.title: Decoding Covert Speech From EEG-A Comprehensive Review
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This is a comprehensive review paper on decoding covert/imagined speech from EEG. While it discusses the same research domain and methodology relevant to inner speech BCI, it does not directly use the openneuro_ds004196 dataset. It reviews various datasets and methods but provides no specific task definition or labels for ds004196.
ref_extractions.super_meta_note: Review discusses EEG-based imagined speech decoding broadly; mentions multiple datasets but does not define a concrete task using ds004196
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: Comprehensive review covering 10+ years of covert speech EEG research; discusses feature extraction, classifiers, electrode configurations; useful context but no direct dataset usage.

ref_extractions.title: Mental imagery of speech and movement implicates the dynamics of internal forward models
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This paper uses MEG to study mental imagery of speech and finger tapping, investigating internal forward models. It is a theoretical/neuroscience study on efference copies and motor planning, not an EEG classification study using the openneuro_ds004196 dataset.
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: MEG-based study on forward models in mental imagery; different modality (MEG vs EEG), different research question, no connection to bimodal inner speech dataset.

ref_extractions.title: Speech and EEG Features for Schizophrenia Detection: Progress and Challenges
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This is a narrative review paper on using speech and EEG features for schizophrenia detection. It discusses speech biomarkers, EEG ERPs, and machine learning for psychiatric diagnosis. It does not involve the openneuro_ds004196 dataset, inner speech classification, or any bimodal EEG-fMRI analysis.
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: Review paper on schizophrenia detection using speech features and EEG biomarkers; completely different research domain from inner speech decoding with healthy subjects.

feasibility_reason: Multiple relevant references (10.1101/2022.05.24.492109 and 10.1038/s41597-023-02286-w) confirm this dataset supports binary Social vs Numeric inner speech classification and 8-class word classification, with trial metadata available via events.tsv sidecar file or derivable from the experimental design structure (40 trials/word, 320 trials/subject).
tasks_section:
## Tasks

### Classical Task 1: Inner Speech Binary Classification (Social vs Numeric)
- **Task Type**: classification
- **Epoch Method**: `epoch_by_segmentation_hdf5`
- **Epoch Parameters**: tmin = -0.1 s, tmax = 2.1 s, segment_length = 2.0 s, overlap = null
- **Label Route**: `event`
- **Meta Level**: raw
- **Target Definition**:
  | Event | y | Meaning |
  |-------|---|---------|
  | `event_111` | 0 | Social word: child |
  | `event_112` | 0 | Social word: daughter |
  | `event_113` | 0 | Social word: father |
  | `event_114` | 0 | Social word: wife |
  | `event_125` | 1 | Numeric word: four |
  | `event_126` | 1 | Numeric word: three |
  | `event_127` | 1 | Numeric word: ten |
  | `event_128` | 1 | Numeric word: six |
- **Evidence**:
  - DOI: 10.1038/s41597-023-02286-w — "Full dataset descriptor defining 8 word stimuli across social (child, daughter, father, wife) and numeric (four, three, ten, six) categories with event IDs 3-10 mapping to word onsets; binary classification task established."
  - DOI: 10.1101/2022.05.24.492109 — "Binary (social vs numeric) classification with Random Forest achieving 62.81% EEG-only accuracy (above 50% chance); 320 trials per subject with 40 trials per word."
- **Kernel Notes**: Read events.tsv sidecar for precise stimulus onset timestamps. Epoch extraction window [-0.1, 2.1]s captures 2s inner speech task period with 100ms baseline. Group events 111-114 as class 0 (social), events 125-128 as class 1 (numeric). 640 social trials and 642 numeric trials total across 4 subjects.

### Classical Task 2: Inner Speech 8-Class Word Classification
- **Task Type**: classification
- **Epoch Method**: `epoch_by_segmentation_hdf5`
- **Epoch Parameters**: tmin = -0.1 s, tmax = 2.1 s, segment_length = 2.0 s, overlap = null
- **Label Route**: `event`
- **Meta Level**: raw
- **Target Definition**:
  | Event | y | Meaning |
  |-------|---|---------|
  | `event_111` | 0 | Social word: child |
  | `event_112` | 1 | Social word: daughter |
  | `event_113` | 2 | Social word: father |
  | `event_114` | 3 | Social word: wife |
  | `event_125` | 4 | Numeric word: four |
  | `event_126` | 5 | Numeric word: three |
  | `event_127` | 6 | Numeric word: ten |
  | `event_128` | 7 | Numeric word: six |
- **Evidence**:
  - DOI: 10.1038/s41597-023-02286-w — "Dataset contains 8 distinct word stimuli with event IDs mapped to each word (3=child, 4=daughter, 5=father, 6=wife, 7=four, 8=three, 9=ten, 10=six) for multiclass classification."
  - DOI: 10.1101/2022.05.24.492109 — "Multiclass (8 words) classification with Random Forest achieving 22.19% accuracy (above 12.5% chance); 40 trials per word per subject."
- **Kernel Notes**: Requires events.tsv sidecar with trial-level timing to distinguish individual word identities. Each word has ~160 trials across 4 subjects. Consider data augmentation or longer segments if baseline performance is insufficient. Trial structure: 1s fixation → 2s task → 1s rest per trial.

### Potential Task 3: Continuous EEG Segmentation (Exploratory)
- **Task Type**: classification
- **Epoch Method**: `epoch_by_long_event_hdf5`
- **Epoch Parameters**: tmin = 0.0 s, tmax = 20.0 s, segment_length = 4.0 s, overlap = 0.5
- **Label Route**: `event`
- **Meta Level**: raw
- **Target Definition**:
  | Event | y | Meaning |
  |-------|---|---------|
  | `event_1` | 0 | Fixation baseline (1282 occurrences) |
  | `event_2` | 1 | Inter-trial rest period (1280 occurrences) |
- **Evidence**:
  - DOI: 10.1101/2022.05.24.492109 — "Preprocessing pipeline uses stimulus timing from E-Prime protocols; continuous segmentation provides alternative approach when precise stimulus onsets are unavailable."
- **Kernel Notes**: Alternative for exploratory analysis without explicit trial timing. Uses fixation (event_1) and rest (event_2) markers to create 4s windows with 50% overlap. Preserves trial structure for subject-level classification. Useful if events.tsv sidecar is corrupted or missing.
